content: Zhang Zhongjing, formally known as Zhang Ji, was a prominent physician during the Eastern Han dynasty, living approximately from 150 to 219 CE. He is widely regarded as one of the most influential figures in the history of Chinese medicine. Zhang established foundational principles of medical practice and synthesized the medicinal knowledge of his time, significantly advancing the development of Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM). Although he is celebrated in modern Chinese medicine, little is known about his life. According to historical accounts, Zhang was born in Nanyang and held an official position in Changsha. The exact dates of his birth, death, and works remain uncertain, though it is generally accepted that he lived until around 220 CE. During his lifetime, the region was plagued by widespread febrile diseases, exacerbated by the political instability and territorial conflicts of the era. Zhang's own family was not spared from these illnesses, which motivated him to study medicine. Zhang Zhongjing learned medicine under the guidance of his fellow townsman Zhang Bozu. He also studied earlier medical texts and collected numerous prescriptions from various sources. His dedication culminated in the creation of his medical masterpiece, the Shanghan Zabing Lun (Treatise on Cold Pathogenic and Miscellaneous Diseases). Unfortunately, this seminal work was lost shortly after its publication due to wartime turmoil. Zhang's contributions to TCM earned him the title of the Sage of Chinese Medicine. His Shanghan Zabing Lun was later reconstructed and divided into two influential texts: the Shang Han Lun (On Cold Damage), which focused on treating epidemic febrile diseases prevalent during his time, and the Jinkui Yaolue (Essential Prescriptions of the Golden Coffer), a comprehensive collection of his clinical experiences. These texts have undergone multiple reconstructions over the centuries and remain foundational in TCM. Zhang Zhongjing is revered as the founder of the Cold Damage or Cold Disease school of Chinese medicine. His work continues to be regarded as a cornerstone of TCM, and he is celebrated as a seminal expert in the field to this day.
